editorial.description: Choe uses scraping, collage and finger painting as metaphors for removing accumulated emotional dirt, moving through a *Titanic* joke, naming current emotions and treating the artist—not the tool—as the vehicle for change.
editorial.summary: Choe uses scraping, collage and finger painting as metaphors for removing accumulated emotional dirt, moving through a *Titanic* joke, naming current emotions and treating the artist—not the tool—as the vehicle for change. This is an official-channel creative lesson or reflection, not clinical treatment or a universal formula. Its chronological map follows the route's own transcript and distinguishes art-making instructions from autobiographical claims, jokes and metaphors. Visually dependent technique still requires the source video.

chapters.title: Closer to the heart, not finished

connections.note: The route uses a studio art process to organize autobiographical reflection; metaphor is part of the exercise and is not medical advice.
The video treats revision, imperfection and emotional attention as more important than copying a polished Choe image.

publication_restrictions.rule: Do not present mental-health, addiction or trauma metaphors as diagnosis or treatment; preserve them as the artist’s framing.

source_notes: Focus and chapter beats were reviewed against this route transcript.
The transcript cannot fully encode tools, color changes, gestures or the developing canvas; use the source video for technique replication.
Claims about personal history remain attributed to Choe.
editorial.speaker_policy: David Choe is the public route-level presenter. Off-camera voices remain unnamed without validated diarization.
